title: ASCII Planet Backdrops
backronym: Eight Claude desktop-app backdrop mods that draw the Sun, the Moon and the planets in ASCII characters.
lede: Each mod paints one body (or one a day) slowly turning behind the conversation, drawn with text characters picked by brightness. This page shows how it works, where it stands, and previews of two proposed upgrades: dithering and edge-shaped characters.

sections.title: Start here: the idea in plain words

blocks.text: The Claude desktop app lets a mod draw a picture behind the chat. These mods draw a planet out of text characters, the way old terminals drew pictures: a dim spot gets a light character like `.` and a bright spot a heavy one like `@`.

There are seven bodies (Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Earth, Saturn), each as its own mod, plus a **week** mod that shows the body of the day: the Sun on Sunday through Saturn on Saturday. `/world <body>` switches by hand.
The picture is drawn on the graphics card every frame. Earth is lit by the real sun for the current time and shows city lights at night; the Moon shows today's real phase.
Published at [github.com/bluetyde/ascii-planet-backdrops](https://github.com/bluetyde/ascii-planet-backdrops) under the MIT licence. All map data is public domain (NASA, USGS, Natural Earth).

items: **A small font.** Each character is a 5 x 7 grid of dots, drawn by hand in `tools/build.mjs`.
**Ink.** Each character's ink is how many of its 35 dots are on: `.` has 1, `@` has 21.
**The ladder.** Characters sorted by ink, one per ink amount, give 12 steps from light to heavy.
**Per cell.** The shader works out how bright each character cell should be (sunlight, the map's colour, darkening toward the edge) and picks the matching step. The cell's colour comes from the map.

blocks.text: Because only brightness picks the character, smooth gradients turn into rings of one character each, and outlines are never drawn on purpose. The two upgrades below address exactly that.

sections.title: Watch it turn: the chosen style
sections.intro: The owner picked the third column: **dithering + outline**. Each animation is one full turn of the body in that style, sped up to 3.6 seconds (24 frames, 0.15 s each). Frames come from the build's still renderer at 24 evenly spaced times (`node tools/build.mjs <data> --animate`), screenshotted in Edge and joined into animated WebP.

sections.title: All four styles compared
sections.intro: Each strip shows one body four ways, left to right: **before** (today's mods), **dithering**, **dithering + outline**, **dithering + outline + inner edges**. These are the still pictures from the build's preview mode (`node tools/build.mjs <data> --preview`), screenshotted in Edge at 640 x 640 and scaled down. The live shader would look the same apart from motion.

blocks.caption: Sun. Dithering softens the rings from the darker edge; the outline traces the disc; inner edges only ring the sunspot.
Moon (still at a gibbous phase). The outline shows the whole disc, dark side included; inner edges trace the maria.
Jupiter. Inner edges draw lines of `_` and `-` along the band borders: the most changed of the seven.
Earth. Inner edges trace the coastlines; dithering breaks up the bright band of sea around the sun's glint.
Saturn. Inner edges fill the rings with slashes, which looks busy; dithering and the outline alone look cleaner.

items: **Edge clutter.** Inner edges help Earth's coastlines but crowd Saturn's rings and stripe Jupiter. The threshold (`EDGE_STEP = 4` glyph levels) may need to differ by body.

**Two copies clash.** A dev copy and an installed copy with the same mod name: the installed one wins, and with different names both run and the one whose day it is draws over the other. Keep one copy installed.
**Moving edges.** On a turning body, coastlines and band edges move, so their characters change as they pass. At one turn per 150 to 600 seconds this stays far below the app's flashing limit.
**Time zone.** The week mod's day uses the mod runtime's clock; if that runs in UTC, the switch happens at UTC midnight. Not yet checked.

items: Backdrop
The picture the Claude desktop app draws behind the conversation; a mod can set it.
Mod
A small plugin that changes Claude's own interface; here, one that sets a theme and draws a backdrop.
Shader
A small program run on the graphics card for every frame; it draws the moving planet.
Cell
One character's box on screen, 9 x 13.5 points, holding 6 x 9 dots.
Ink
How many of a character's 35 dots are on; more ink looks brighter.
Ramp
The ladder of characters sorted by ink, from `.` to `@`.
Dithering
Nudging each cell's brightness by a small fixed amount so neighbouring cells mix two steps instead of forming hard bands.
Edge character
A character chosen for its shape, such as `/` or `|`, placed where brightness changes sharply, along the edge's direction.
Index map
The body's map drawn in colours one or two steps off black, invisible to the eye; the shader reads each colour back as a number and looks up the real colour.
Libration
The Moon's slow wobble as seen from Earth; the Moon mod rocks instead of spinning.

entries.status: Dithering + outline ported to the shaders; 0.4.0 published.
body: Changed: `src/body.shader.ts` (Bayer dither in `level`, outline from the disc angle, glyph field /31), `tools/build.mjs` (outline glyph bitmaps, dither + outline as the default), all 8 mods rebuilt at 0.4.0.

Verified: build checks pass; all 8 mods and the marketplace pass `claude plugin validate` (cell pass about 1.3 ms, picture 3.8 ms on weak GPUs); owner saw the outline live on the Moon, Mars and other bodies through a renamed dev copy.
Caveats: Earth was not seen live with the outline, because the old installed copy drew over it; its shader holds the same code as the others.
